items.title: 13.7 Relative reactivity of halide ions as reducing agents (reducing agents ke taur par halide ions ka muqabla) (Roman Urdu)

source_refs.note: Roman Urdu explanation of topic 13.7, printed page 297.

blocks.text: Halide ions ki reducing ability (doosre ko electron de kar reduce karne ki ability) group mein fluorine se iodine tak neeche jate hue barhti hai. Is ki bari wajah yeh hai ke neeche jate hue electronegativity (electron ko apni taraf kheenchne ki taqat) kam hoti hai aur atomic radius barhta hai. Is se charge density (ion ke size ke muqable mein charge ka jamaao) kam hoti hai aur electron dena aasan ho jata hai. Halides mein fluoride ion sab se weak (kamzor) aur iodide sab se strong (taqatwar) reducing agent hai.
Reducing agent ke taur par kam hoti power ka order (tarteeb) yeh hai: I⁻ > Br⁻ > Cl⁻ > F⁻. Neeche har ion ki properties se is trend ki explanation (wazahat) hai.

Fluorine ki electronegativity bohat zyada hai aur fluorine atom apne extra (faltu) electron ko zor se pakarta hai, is liye fluoride ion (F⁻) ke liye electron dena mushkil hai. Fluoride ion chhota hai, is liye is ki charge density zyada hai; yeh ion ko aur stable karti hai aur electron khone ki tendency (jhukao) kam karti hai.
Chloride ion (Cl⁻) fluoride se strong reducing agent hai, lekin bromide aur iodide se ab bhi weak hai. Wajah: is ka size bara aur electronegativity kam hai.

Bromide (Br⁻) chloride se strong reducing agent hai. Bromine chlorine se kam electronegative hai. Bromide ion (Br⁻) ka ionic radius bara aur charge density kam hai, is liye yeh aasani se electron kho deta hai aur reducing agent ka kaam karta hai.

Iodide (I⁻) chloride aur bromide dono se bohat strong reducing agent hai. Iodine ki electronegativity chlorine aur bromine se bohat kam hai, aur iodide ion (I⁻) size mein bara hai. Is liye is ki charge density kam hai aur yeh aasani se electron de deta hai; yahi ise strong reducing agent banata hai.

blocks.title: Easy words mein
blocks.text: Halogen molecule (X₂) aur halide ion (X⁻) ulte chalte hain: F₂ sab se strong oxidizing agent hai (electron sab se aasani se leta hai), is liye F⁻ apna electron sab se mushkil se chhorta hai aur sab se weak reducing agent hai. I₂ sab se weak oxidizing agent hai, is liye I⁻ sab se strong reducing agent hai.

blocks.prompt: F⁻ Cl⁻ se weak reducing agent kyun hai?
blocks.explanation: Fluorine sab se zyada electronegative hai aur F⁻ bohat chhota hai, is liye is ka extra electron nucleus ke qareeb zor se pakra hota hai (charge density zyada). Cl⁻ bara hai aur chlorine kam electronegative hai, is liye is ka electron dheela hai aur aasani se diya ja sakta hai.

items: Reducing taqat: I⁻ > Br⁻ > Cl⁻ > F⁻.
Neeche jate hue electronegativity kam, radius zyada, charge density kam: electron dena aasan.
